threads.title: The Access Log
threads.intro: Find what is missing and what a door controller can actually tell you.
threads.outcome_text: The access-token envelope is gone, and the door log proves a badge was used, not who carried it.

threads.title: The Borrowed Identity
threads.intro: Follow B-204 through checkout, return and the next custody event, and test the cable request.
threads.outcome_text: Ishaan returned the badge before the entry, and the cable request does not link Arjun to the archive.

threads.title: What Was Really Taken?
threads.intro: Compare the inventory notes and messages with the badge custody trail.
threads.outcome_text: Maya’s custody, amended note and messages fit together and explain the interference.

story_events.title: A badge, not a face
story_events.body: The archive count drops from one to zero between 18:05 and 18:21. The controller logs badge B-204 entering at 18:17 and notes that it records the badge ID only.

story_events.title: Signed back in
story_events.body: Dev accepts the signed return of B-204 at 17:24. Maya takes the badge for a temporary scan at 17:31 and no return to the desk follows. Arjun’s cable came from the AV cabinet.

story_events.title: An amended note
story_events.body: At 18:11 Maya amends the note to say the return is unconfirmed. Dev’s later verification says the signed return was accepted at 17:24 and that the later note conflicts with the desk record.
